name: WV-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Carol Miller running with large fundraising edge
No polls or expert ratings; fundamentals and markets both point heavily Republican
Polymarket prices Democratic win at just 2%
model.rationale: The baseline's -18.9 margin rests on a strong R+22 partisan lean, Miller's incumbency and 7-to-1 fundraising advantage, with no contrary evidence in polls, ratings, or headlines. I stay essentially at the baseline, nudged only slightly by the prediction market's 98% Republican pricing.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement would be the main path to moving this race toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's 1st District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+22. Incumbent Carol Miller is seeking reelection after easily securing her party's nomination, and she holds a substantial financial advantage over Democratic nominee Vince George, having raised roughly seven times as much money.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert ratings for this race, so the forecast relies on fundamentals: the district's lean, Miller's incumbency bonus, and the fundraising gap. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 2% chance of an upset. All available evidence points to a comfortable Republican win, and the race is rated Safe R.
